_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4469 / req 2d072437-c19d-49a4-ae89-f20b6185571f — FrontmatterService, the TEXT write channel behind `set-property`, `remove-property`, `set-body` and every `apply <cmd>` that writes a property. Each mutant removes ONE guarantee and must redden EXACTLY the axes that state it; expectations written BEFORE the run. M1/M6/M7 restore the pre-#4469 LF-only predicate at each of its three sites (they were three separate call sites, not one, so three mutants); M2 models a js-yaml RE-DUMP of the block (the thing decision 1 of the requirement forbids — it costs LF/CRLF assets their byte-identity while leaving the block count correct, which is why it reddens the byte-shape axes and NOT CH1); M3/M4 pin the two halves of the BOM policy (a run collapses to one; a single one is not dropped); M5 pins that a newly inserted line carries the FILE's line ending rather than LF.

M1_updateProperty_back_to_lf_only_predic._note: The exact predicate this class carried until #4469. A non-LF (or BOM-prefixed) asset is then seen as having no block, so updateProperty PREPENDS a second one — the measured defect. CH5 (pure LF) stays green, which is the control that the mutant is not simply breaking everything.

M2_body_rejoined_with_lf_like_a_redump._note: Models the js-yaml RE-DUMP `updateProperty` must NOT become: the block comes back with one uniform LF ending and the original bytes are gone. The block COUNT stays correct, so CH1 and CH3 stay green — the mutant is pointed at byte-identity alone, which is what decision 1 of the requirement is about.

M3_bom_run_preserved_verbatim._note: Keeps N BOMs instead of collapsing to one. CH6 (a single BOM) stays green — a run and a single byte are different halves of the policy and each has its own axis.

M4_bom_dropped_entirely._note: The opposite failure: the write silently re-encodes a file the user deliberately marked. Both BOM axes redden.
